examples.trans: It's winter.

examples.text: En hiver, il fait froid.
examples.trans: In winter it's cold.

meanings.note: Before a noun it can mean only; after a person it often means alone.

examples.text: Il est seul.
examples.trans: He is alone.

examples.text: C'est notre seul allié.
examples.trans: He is our only ally.

meanings.note: Neighbourhood shop selling tools, screws, and valves.

examples.text: J'ai utilisé la dernière cet hiver. Seule la vieille quincaillerie après le pont vend cette taille.
examples.trans: I used the last one this winter. Only the old hardware shop past the bridge sells this size.

examples.text: À quelle heure ouvre cette quincaillerie?
examples.trans: What time does that hardware shop open?

examples.text: C'est fait. Maintenant, expliquez-moi comment trouver la quincaillerie.
examples.trans: Got it. Now explain to me how to find the hardware shop.

meanings.note: Après le déjeuner.

examples.text: Après, elles ne peuvent plus s'arrêter.
examples.trans: Then they can't stop anymore.

examples.text: On mange, et après on part.
examples.trans: We eat, and afterwards we leave.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le pont', plural 'les ponts') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'bridge'.

examples.text: Le pont, puis la pharmacie verte à droite. Et ensuite?
examples.trans: The bridge, then the green pharmacy on the right. And next?

examples.text: À gauche au portail, tout droit jusqu'au pont. Je traverse le fleuve?
examples.trans: Left at the gate, straight ahead to the bridge. Do I cross the river?

meanings.note: Sell; past participle vendu, with avoir in compound tenses.

examples.text: Je veux vendre.
examples.trans: I want to sell.

examples.text: Il vend des fleurs.
examples.trans: He sells flowers.

examples.text: Avec grand plaisir, Thibault, tant que personne ne parle de vendre de vieux pianos!
examples.trans: With great pleasure, Thibault, as long as nobody talks about selling old pianos!

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la taille', plural 'les tailles') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'size'.
Feminine noun ('la taille', plural 'les tailles') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'height'.
Feminine noun ('la taille', plural 'les tailles') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'waist'.

examples.text: Quelle est votre taille de pantalon?
examples.trans: What is your trouser size?

examples.text: Une personne de grande taille.
examples.trans: A tall person.

examples.text: J'ai utilisé la dernière cet hiver. Seule la vieille quincaillerie après le pont vend cette taille.
examples.trans: I used the last one this winter. Only the old hardware shop past the bridge sells this size.

meanings.note: Agrees with the noun.
Quelle surprise!.

examples.text: Quelle heure est-il? Neuf heures trente-cinq!
examples.trans: What time is it? Nine thirty-five!

examples.text: Quelle vitesse! L'épicier vous a donné un ticket?
examples.trans: What speed! Did the grocer give you a receipt?

meanings.note: Dans une heure = in an hour.
À quatorze heures = at two pm.

examples.text: À onze heures.
examples.trans: At eleven o'clock.

examples.text: Quelle heure est-il? Neuf heures trente-cinq!
examples.trans: What time is it? Nine thirty-five!

meanings.en: to open (a door, eyes, a book)
meanings.note: conjugated like an -er verb in the present tense: j'ouvre, tu ouvres...

examples.text: Ouvre la porte, Julie!
examples.trans: Open the door, Julie!

examples.text: Le magasin ouvre à neuf heures.
examples.trans: The shop opens at nine o'clock.

meanings.note: the p is silent, the t is pronounced

examples.text: Voici votre clé, numéro quatre. Le petit-déjeuner est de sept heures trente à dix heures.
examples.trans: Here is your key, number four. Breakfast is from seven thirty to ten.

examples.text: Huit clients affamés descendent à sept heures et demie!
examples.trans: Eight hungry guests come down at half past seven!

examples.text: Donnez-moi un sac et de l'argent! L'épicerie du coin ouvre à sept heures.
examples.trans: Give me a bag and some cash! The corner grocery shop opens at seven.

meanings.note: Neuf heures pile. Invariable French adverb meaning 'sharp'; placed immediately after the conjugated verb in simple tenses.

examples.text: Il est arrivé à midi pile.
examples.trans: He arrived at noon sharp.

examples.text: Huit heures pile! Notre client est là!
examples.trans: Eight o'clock on the dot! Our guest is here!

examples.text: À sept heures pile, trente minutes avant le petit-déjeuner.
examples.trans: At seven sharp, thirty minutes before breakfast.

examples.text: Elle a trente ans.
examples.trans: She's thirty.

examples.text: Trente euros, s'il vous plaît.
examples.trans: Thirty euros, please.

meanings.note: Cinq minutes = five minutes.

examples.text: Attendez cinq minutes.
examples.trans: Wait five minutes.

examples.text: J'arrive dans une minute.
examples.trans: I'll be there in a minute.

meanings.note: Time: avant mon départ.

examples.text: Dernière réunion avant mon départ.
examples.trans: Last meeting before I leave.

examples.text: Viens avant midi.
examples.trans: Come before noon.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le petit-déjeuner', plural 'les petits-déjeuners') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'morning meal'.

examples.text: Je prends toujours un café au petit-déjeuner.
examples.trans: I always have a coffee at breakfast.

examples.text: On a organisé un petit-déjeuner avec le réalisateur.
examples.trans: We organized a breakfast meeting with the director.

examples.text: Bonne nuit, Claire. À demain au petit-déjeuner.
examples.trans: Good night, Claire. See you tomorrow at breakfast.

examples.text: Règle ça, s'il te plaît.
examples.trans: Sort it out, please.

examples.text: Je vais régler le problème.
examples.trans: I'll sort out the problem.

meanings.note: Régler son réveil = to set one's alarm.

examples.text: Réglez votre réveil, Henri. Demain matin, on gagne contre l'eau froide!
examples.trans: Set your alarm, Henri. Tomorrow morning, we beat the cold water!

examples.text: Voici le réveil sur la table.
examples.trans: Here is the alarm clock on the table.

meanings.note: everyday speech, with a he/she verb form
General.

examples.text: Dans le tiroir. Ici, on utilise ce grand cahier en papier et un crayon.
examples.trans: In the drawer. Here we use this big paper notebook and a pencil.

examples.text: Merci! On se tutoie ici?
examples.trans: Thank you! Do we use casual 'you' here?

examples.text: Asseyez-vous, madame. Ne vous inquiétez pas, on va regarder l'étiquette tout de suite.
examples.trans: Please sit down, madam. Do not worry, we will check the tag right now.

meanings.note: For receiving income or a wage.
For winning a game, competition or prize.

examples.text: Ce que gagne chaque personne.
examples.trans: What each person earns.

examples.text: On a gagné!
examples.trans: We won!

examples.text: Réglez votre réveil, Henri. Demain matin, on gagne contre l'eau froide!
examples.trans: Set your alarm, Henri. Tomorrow morning, we beat the cold water!

meanings.note: Against someone or something; se battre contre, fight against.

examples.text: Je suis contre.
examples.trans: I'm against it.

examples.text: Se battre contre le chagrin.
examples.trans: To fight against sorrow.

examples.text: Réglez votre réveil, Henri. Demain matin, on gagne contre l'eau froide!
examples.trans: Set your alarm, Henri. Tomorrow morning, we beat the cold water!

meanings.en: cold (adjective); avoir froid = to feel cold; il fait froid = it's cold

examples.text: J'ai froid.
examples.trans: I'm cold.

examples.text: J'avais les mains froides sous le choc!
examples.trans: My hands were cold from the shock!
